name: Dextromethorphan

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: DXM/dextrorphan blockade of NMDA receptors reduces glutamate-evoked Ca2+ influx in neurons. Sigma-1 agonism modulates IP3-receptor Ca2+ release from ER and chaperones BiP dissociation, contributing to neuroprotective and antidepressant effects.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Converts EM to phenocopy PM; DXM AUC increases 20-40 fold (basis for Nuedexta DXM/quinidine combo).
Persistent CYP2D6 inhibition (kinact 0.17 min-1); markedly elevated DXM exposure and serotonin syndrome risk.
Increases DXM exposure; documented serotonin syndrome cases with DXM cough syrup + fluoxetine.

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic — DXM SERT inhibition + MAO blockade
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Severe serotonin syndrome and hyperpyrexia; contraindicated combination.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 PMs (~7% of Caucasians, ~1% Asians): 5-fold higher DXM Cmax, t1/2 ~24 h vs ~3 h in EMs, DXO concentrations only 3% of EM values. UMs (CYP2D6 gene duplication) experience minimal subjective dissociation. PMs are at high risk of dose-dependent dissociation and serotonin syndrome at recreational doses; UMs at risk of opioid-like sedation from rapid DXO formation in rare cases.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Reverse tolerance / kindling-like phenomenon reported anecdotally in chronic DXM users (autoinduction of CYP2D6 has been hypothesised but not confirmed in humans).
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Chronic high-dose users may develop psychological dependence with insomnia, dysphoria, craving, mild dysautonomia lasting 1-2 weeks. No major physical withdrawal syndrome.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: QTc prolongation reported with supratherapeutic doses and CYP2D6 inhibitor co-administration; case reports of arrhythmia at recreational doses.
May contribute to anti-addictive effects observed in animal models.

demographic_differences.age: Pediatric DXM clearance higher per kg; recreational paediatric overdose particularly dangerous due to combination products (acetaminophen, chlorpheniramine, pseudoephedrine).
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment expected to increase DXM exposure (CYP2D6-dependent); no formal dedicated study published.

data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative human PET imaging of NMDA channel occupancy at recreational doses
Biased agonism data at sigma-1

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Identical pharmacology to free-base DXM after dissociation in GI tract.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: See Dextromethorphan record — same CYP2D6 dependency.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Chronic high-dose users may experience psychological dependence; bromism (chronic Br- accumulation) may present with neurological/dermatologic signs after years of high-dose use.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Bromism with chronic megadosing — bromide t1/2 ~12 days, replaces Cl-, causes neuropsychiatric symptoms and acneiform rash.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal impairment slows Br- clearance — bromism risk amplified.

name: DXM Polistirex

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Once dissociated from the polistirex ion-exchange resin in GI tract, behaves identically to free-base DXM.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Same as DXM; ER formulation prolongs effect duration in both EMs and PMs.

data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative PK head-to-head comparison vs IR DXM in CYP2D6 PMs

name: Dxme
data_gaps_remaining: No peer-reviewed identification of compound 'Dxme' exists; not found in PubChem, ChEMBL, NPS Discovery, EMCDDA EWS, or Tactogen monographs. Possible misspelling of DXM, DXE (deschloroketamine analogue), or DMXE (3-MeO-2'-Oxo-PCE / methoxmetamine).

name: Memantine

primary_targets: NMDA-receptor (PCP site, low-affinity uncompetitive open-channel blocker)
pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Preferential block of extrasynaptic over synaptic NMDA receptors (Xia et al. 2010, J Neurosci 30:11246) — this selectivity arises from extrasynaptic NMDARs being more frequently activated by low ambient glutamate, allowing memantine's voltage- and use-dependent block to accumulate. Extrasynaptic NMDA activation drives pro-apoptotic CREB shutoff signalling, while synaptic NMDA activation drives pro-survival CREB activation; memantine's bias preserves the latter — the molecular basis for therapeutic utility in Alzheimer's.

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: Urinary pH ↑ → ↑ tubular reabsorption of protonated memantine
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Up to 9-fold increase in memantine plasma concentrations

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic — additive NMDA channel block + OCT2 competition
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Increased risk of CNS toxicity; combination not recommended.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Polymorphisms in OCT2/MATE1 affect tubular secretion; clinically modest. CYP genotype is largely irrelevant given negligible hepatic metabolism.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: May contribute to cognitive side-effects; under investigation.
Possibly contributes to low emetogenic profile vs other NMDA antagonists.
Weak D2 affinity reported; not clinically significant at therapeutic doses.

demographic_differences.sex: Women have ~45% higher AUC at same mg dose (lower body weight + lower renal clearance per kg).
demographic_differences.age: Elderly (target population) have reduced renal function — dose-adjust in CrCl 5-29 mL/min to 5 mg BID.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal impairment markedly increases exposure: mean AUC ↑ 4%, 60%, 115% in mild, moderate, severe renal impairment respectively. t1/2 increases up to 95%. Hepatic impairment: negligible effect (no CYP dependence).

data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative human NMDA receptor occupancy at therapeutic vs recreational dose ranges (no PET ligand routine for this)

name: Diphenidine

functional.readout: fluorescence uptake inhibition (HEK293 stably expressing hDAT)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Use- and voltage-dependent NMDA channel blockade; slower kinetic off-rate than memantine giving extended dissociation (anecdotal duration 4-6 h orally). Weak DA reuptake inhibition may contribute to stimulant overlay reported by users.

metabolism.enzyme: CYP3A4/CYP2C19 (presumed, by analogy and metabolite profiling)

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Reverse tolerance and cravings reported anecdotally in heavy users; no controlled data.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Anecdotal reports of insomnia, dysphoria, craving, anxiety; not formally characterised.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: May contribute to affective overlay similar to DXM.

data_gaps_remaining: No controlled human PK study (no Cmax/Tmax/t1/2 published)
No biased-agonism / functional NMDA on-off kinetic data
No quantitative tolerance / withdrawal characterisation

name: Methoxphenidine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Voltage- and use-dependent NMDA channel block. The 2-methoxy substitution reduces affinity vs diphenidine but does not fundamentally change the binding pose. The 3-methoxy isomer (3-MeO-PCP-like geometry) is substantially more potent (Ki 19 nM); the 4-methoxy isomer collapses to Ki 461 nM — a steep SAR demonstrating the importance of meta-substitution on the aryl ring for PCP-site engagement.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Anecdotal rapid tolerance; cross-tolerance to ketamine reported.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Moderate affinity reported in Wallach screen.

data_gaps_remaining: No controlled human pharmacokinetic data
No information on isomeric purity of street samples (2-MXP vs 3-MXP — pharmacologically very different)
No biased-agonism / electrophysiology kinetics

name: Ephenidine

functional.readout: field EPSP in rat hippocampal CA1 (theta-burst stimulation)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Voltage-dependent channel block similar to ketamine; 10 μM ephenidine blocks LTP induction by theta-burst stimulation in rat hippocampal slices, consistent with synaptic plasticity disruption underlying anti-depressant-like effects of NMDA antagonists.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK data
No metabolism / CYP characterisation
No biased-agonism data

name: 2-chloro-ephenidine

primary_targets: NMDA receptor (PCP site, presumed by structural analogy)

data_gaps_remaining: No peer-reviewed pharmacology — no binding, functional, PK, or metabolism data
No formal toxicology / case reports

name: 2-TFMXP
data_gaps_remaining: No published Ki/IC50 at any target
No human PK or toxicology
Not catalogued in Wallach 2016 series

name: Fluorolintane

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Notable feature: DAT affinity is higher than NMDA affinity for fluorolintane — among the diarylethylamines, this profile is the closest approximation to a 'dissociative-stimulant' hybrid; users report substantial arousal vs the more dissociative-typical diphenidine.

data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative DAT/NET/SERT Ki values for fluorolintane specifically
No human PK data
Limited toxicology

name: Dizocilpine

binding.tissue_or_cell: rat cerebral cortical membrane / rat whole brain

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Trapping channel blocker — channel can close while drug is inside, requiring re-opening for drug egress. This trapping mechanism produces durable blockade and underlies both the long behavioural duration and the Olney's-lesion neurotoxicity (excessive disinhibition of cortical glutamate -> heat-shock response in retrosplenial neurons).

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Tolerance develops within days of repeated dosing in animals; NMDA receptor upregulation following chronic blockade documented (Williams et al.).
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: No clinical syndrome described in humans (limited exposure). Animal studies show rebound hyperexcitability and seizure threshold reduction.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Originally claimed as sigma ligand; subsequent work shows the apparent sigma binding was actually low-affinity off-target — dizocilpine is highly selective for the NMDA PCP site.

data_gaps_remaining: Modern published human PK study

name: Nitrous

binding.tissue_or_cell: cultured rat hippocampal neurons; Xenopus oocytes expressing NR1/NR2 subunits
binding.radioligand_or_probe: Whole-cell NMDA currents; inhibition >50% at 80% atm N2O at -60 mV

binding.action: indirect agonist via endogenous enkephalin/dynorphin release in periaqueductal grey (PAG)
binding.radioligand_or_probe: Microdialysis of enkephalin / antinociception blockade by naloxone

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Dual mechanism: (1) NMDA channel blockade driving rapid-onset dissociation, euphoria, and (when sustained) Olney's lesions; (2) Endogenous opioid release in PAG driving analgesia via descending noradrenergic pathways. The opioid arm explains why N2O analgesia is reversed by naloxone and why it shows cross-tolerance with morphine. Antidepressant effects (Nagele et al. 2015, 2021) likely driven by NMDA antagonism analogous to ketamine. Recent literature also implicates two-pore K+ channels (TREK-1) and modest HCN1 inhibition in anaesthetic effects.

neuroimaging.finding: N2O at sub-anesthetic concentrations produces increased BOLD in anterior cingulate cortex and posterior cingulate cortex with reduced default-mode network connectivity — pattern overlapping with ketamine.

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: Oxidation of MeCbl Co1+ → Co3+ inactivates methionine synthase
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Megaloblastic anaemia; subacute combined degeneration of cord; sensorimotor neuropathy. Onset over weeks to months of heavy use; cases reported with chronic ~10 canister/day use.
Increased risk of bone marrow suppression and neurotoxicity.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: MTHFR C677T TT homozygotes have lower baseline methionine synthase activity and are at elevated risk of N2O-induced neurotoxicity. Hyperhomocysteinaemia-associated genetic variants compound the risk.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Rapid acute tolerance (tachyphylaxis) within a single session of repeated balloons due to brief PK exposure. Tolerance to euphoria reported in heavy users.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild psychological dependence; craving, dysphoria, occasional autonomic hyperactivity in chronic heavy users. No prominent physical withdrawal.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Modest inhibition may contribute to anaesthetic and analgesic effects.

demographic_differences.age: Adolescents and young adults overrepresented in recreational use case series; rapid onset of myelopathy in heavy users <25 y.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: No meaningful effect — pulmonary excretion bypasses both.

data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative NMDA NR2 subtype selectivity
Direct human in-vivo NMDA occupancy measurement
Dose-response curve for B12 inactivation in humans

name: Ibogaine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Multi-target polypharmacology with no single dominant mechanism. NMDA channel block (low-μM) acts synergistically with kappa-opioid G-biased agonism (via metabolite noribogaine) and SERT inhibition. The 'iboga experience' itself may reflect transient combined NMDA antagonism + 5-HT2A agonism (oneirogenic visions); the sub-acute anti-addictive effect (days-weeks) likely reflects the long-acting noribogaine metabolite acting at kappa-opioid and SERT.

routes.subject_demographics: Glue et al. healthy volunteer ascending dose study; mixed CYP2D6 genotype

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: 2-fold increase in active moiety (ibogaine + noribogaine) exposure; markedly increased cardiotoxicity risk.
Severe QTc prolongation, torsades risk — absolutely contraindicated combinations.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 PMs have markedly higher and longer-lasting ibogaine exposure → higher cardiotoxicity risk. UMs have rapid clearance → less effect at standard doses but rapid noribogaine accumulation. PM genotype is essentially a contraindication for full-dose ibogaine without dose adjustment.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: No conventional tolerance described — ibogaine is typically dosed once or in widely spaced 're-treatments'. No physical dependence syndrome.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: QTc prolongation, torsades-de-pointes, sudden cardiac death. The dominant lethal hazard. Documented at standard anti-addictive doses (8-10 mg/kg) in healthy individuals without pre-existing cardiac disease.

demographic_differences.weight: mg/kg dosing standard; very high doses (>20 mg/kg) approach lethal range.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment increases exposure due to CYP2D6 dependency.

data_gaps_remaining: Functional NMDA receptor electrophysiology (open vs trapping block, on/off kinetics)
Quantitative human PET imaging of NMDA / kappa-opioid / SERT occupancy
Mechanistic dissection of which target drives which subjective effect

class_name: Non-arylcyclohexylamine NMDA receptor antagonists (morphinans, aminoadamantanes, dibenzocycloheptenes, anaesthetic gases)
shared_mechanism: Heterogeneous chemotypes that converge on the NMDA receptor PCP / channel-binding site, blocking the open channel in a use- and voltage-dependent manner. Affinity ranges from very low (DXM ~7 μM at the parent; dextrorphan metabolite ~0.9 μM) through low-affinity fast-off-rate (memantine, amantadine ~1-10 μM IC50, koff ~5 s-1) to extremely high-affinity slow-trapping (MK-801 Ki ~2 nM, koff ~0.01 s-1). Off-target serotonergic, sigma, nicotinic, and HCN1 actions vary by scaffold and explain qualitative differences in subjective profile — DXM is ketamine-adjacent with serotonergic affective overlay; memantine is functionally subtler due to fast off-rate and extrasynaptic selectivity; MK-801 is uncontrolled-dissociative with Olney's-lesion neurotoxicity. Nitrous oxide is mechanistically related (NMDA antagonist) but is the outlier in route (gas), kinetics (5-min onset/offset), and chronic toxicity (irreversible B12 inactivation).
shared_pk_summary: DXM: oral, CYP2D6-dominated metabolism to active dextrorphan, F% varies 1-80% between PMs and EMs. Memantine: oral F 100%, ~100% renal-cleared (active tubular secretion + pH-dependent reabsorption), t1/2 60-80 h, no meaningful CYP role. Amantadine: similar profile to memantine but t1/2 ~17 h. MK-801: research tool, no published modern human PK. Nitrous: pulmonary, blood-gas 0.47, pharmacokinetics dominated by alveolar ventilation; non-metabolised (except for irreversible MTR-cobalamin oxidation, which is mechanistically a poison reaction not a clearance pathway).
shared_safety: Acute: respiratory depression (NMDA antagonists are normally respiratory-sparing but in massive overdose or with synergistic CNS depressants this fails); psychotomimetic effects (Olney's lesions on chronic high-dose for slow-off compounds — MK-801, PCP, ketamine; not seen with fast-off memantine at therapeutic doses). DXM specific: hERG block + SERT activity → QT prolongation + serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs/MAOIs (Nuedexta DXM/quinidine combination exploits the CYP2D6-driven exposure boost). Nitrous specific: irreversible B12 inactivation → subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord with chronic heavy use (cases reliable at multi-canister-per-day exposure).
sar_summary: Across this heterogeneous group, the unifying SAR axis is fit to the PCP/channel binding pocket. Within each scaffold: (1) morphinans — the dextrorotatory enantiomer is the NMDA-active series; CH2OMe vs OH at C3 (DXM vs DXO) changes affinity ~10x; (2) aminoadamantanes — methyl substitution on the adamantane cage (amantadine → memantine = 3,5-dimethyl) raises affinity ~10x and slightly slows off-rate but retains fast koff and voltage-dependent block; (3) dibenzocycloheptenes (MK-801) — methyl-bridged rigid scaffold maximises affinity and slows off-rate dramatically; (4) gases (N2O, xenon) — molecular volume and lipophilicity govern channel-pocket interaction. The fast-off vs slow-off distinction within the PCP site is more clinically important than absolute affinity — slow-off compounds are neurotoxic and psychotomimetic; fast-off are tolerable.

shared_mechanism: Open-chain (non-cyclic) NMDA channel blockers built on a 1,2-diphenyl-ethylamine scaffold with a cyclic amine on the alpha-carbon. Bind the PCP site of the NMDA receptor with high to moderate affinity (Ki 9-460 nM range, Wallach et al. 2016) in a use- and voltage-dependent manner. (S)-enantiomer is the active form (~40x more potent than R). Off-target profile: weak-to-moderate dopamine/norepinephrine reuptake inhibition (more prominent in pyrrolidine analogues like fluorolintane), moderate sigma-1/sigma-2 binding, generally negligible SERT and opioid receptor affinity (unlike DXM, which has appreciable SERT). The 1,2-diaryl orientation and lack of cyclohexyl ring distinguish them structurally from arylcyclohexylamines like PCP/ketamine, but they share the same NMDA binding pose and similar voltage-dependent block kinetics.
shared_pk_summary: No controlled human PK studies have been published for any diphenidine-class compound. Forensic toxicology of intoxications and fatalities (Helander et al. 2015; Elliott et al. 2015; Geyer et al. 2015) shows: oral and insufflated routes both used; duration of subjective effects 4-8 h depending on compound; primary urinary metabolites are ring-hydroxylated and N-dealkylated products (CYP-mediated, presumed CYP3A4/2C19); no specific quantitative human Cmax, Tmax, t1/2 published. Postmortem blood concentrations of MXP in fatalities span ~200 μg/L to 24 mg/L — wide range indicates substantial inter-individual variability and a narrow therapeutic index.
shared_safety: Major risks: (1) Narrow therapeutic index — multiple documented fatalities for MXP and diphenidine; recreational doses are close to toxic doses. (2) Long duration (4-8+ h) facilitates additional dosing during plateau, leading to delayed cumulative toxicity. (3) Co-ingestion with other CNS depressants (alcohol, benzodiazepines, GHB) is the most common fatal scenario. (4) Hypertensive crises, tachycardia, agitation, and dissociative psychosis reported in clinical case series. (5) No characterised antidote — supportive management only. (6) Cross-tolerance with ketamine reported anecdotally. Isomeric purity is a forensic concern: 3-MeO-diphenidine is ~2x more potent than 2-MeO at NMDA (Ki 19 vs 36 nM), and street 'MXP' has occasionally been the 3-MeO isomer or contained it as a contaminant.
sar_summary: Key SAR findings from Wallach et al. 2016 (PLOS One): (1) NMDA affinity sensitive to ortho/meta vs para position of substituents on the 'aryl A' ring: meta-OMe (3-MXP) ≈ unsubstituted (DPH) > ortho-OMe (2-MXP) >> para-OMe (4-MXP); (2) Halogen at the 2-position dramatically increases affinity: 2-Cl-DPH Ki 9.3 nM (~2x parent), and the chloro analogue of ephenidine (2-Cl-ephenidine) is predicted to follow same trend; (3) Pyrrolidine (5-ring) replacing piperidine (6-ring) on nitrogen reduces NMDA affinity but markedly increases DAT inhibition — fluorolintane shows DAT > NMDA affinity, the opposite of the piperidine series; (4) Open-chain secondary amine (ephenidine, NEDPA) reduces affinity ~3x vs cyclic piperidine but retains channel-blocker mechanism. Conformational restriction by the cyclic amine on nitrogen is favourable for NMDA channel docking. CF3 substitution (2-TFMXP, no published Ki) remains pharmacologically uncharacterised but would predict either potent affinity (electron-withdrawing analogous to halogen) or steric loss depending on pocket geometry.

shared_mechanism: Indolealkylamine monoterpenoid alkaloids from Tabernanthe iboga, with an unusually broad polypharmacology: weak-to-moderate affinity at NMDA receptors (Ki ~1-3 μM at PCP site), kappa-opioid (Ki ~0.7-3 μM, G-protein-biased agonism for noribogaine), mu-opioid (Ki ~2-5 μM, weak functional antagonism for noribogaine), serotonin transporter (Ki 40-550 nM, with noribogaine 10x more potent), sigma-1/sigma-2, 5-HT2A weak agonism, alpha3-beta4 nicotinic, and hERG (IC50 3.5 μM for ibogaine — clinically important arrhythmia risk). The anti-addictive efficacy is thought to arise from combined NMDA antagonism (Glick & Maisonneuve 1998), kappa-opioid G-biased agonism (Maillet et al. 2015), and SERT inhibition (especially via noribogaine). Pharmacology is not driven by any one target but by the orchestrated multi-target profile.
shared_pk_summary: Ibogaine: oral, CYP2D6-dominated metabolism to noribogaine. Ibogaine plasma t1/2 ~7 h in EMs (shorter in UMs, much longer in PMs). Cmax and AUC strongly CYP2D6-genotype-dependent (Glue et al. 2015 — r=0.77 for Cmax). Noribogaine: t1/2 28-49 h (long-acting; persists days after parent gone — likely the species responsible for sub-acute mood and craving effects). Noribogaine itself has been formally characterised in healthy volunteers (Glue et al. 2014 ascending dose study).
shared_safety: PRIMARY ACUTE RISK: cardiac arrhythmia. Ibogaine blocks hERG (IC50 3.5 μM) and prolongs QTc; multiple case reports of fatal torsades-de-pointes at treatment doses (8-10 mg/kg). Pre-existing QT prolongation, hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, structural heart disease, CYP2D6 PM genotype (slower metabolism, higher exposure), and concomitant QT-prolonging drugs all amplify risk. ECG monitoring, electrolyte repletion, and avoidance of co-medications are mandatory in clinical use. SUB-ACUTE: dystonia, ataxia, vomiting (24-72h), and prolonged dysregulation of mood. Cerebellar Purkinje cell toxicity seen in rats at very high doses (no clear human correlate). Noribogaine appears better tolerated cardiovascularly than parent ibogaine.
sar_summary: Ibogaine → noribogaine (O-demethyl metabolite) is the dominant SAR shift: removing the 12-methoxy group of ibogaine to free phenol (noribogaine) (1) increases SERT affinity 10x (Ki 550 → 40 nM), (2) modestly increases opioid receptor affinities (Ki kappa 2.6 → 0.72 μM, mu 5 → 2.7 μM), (3) reduces NMDA affinity, (4) profoundly extends half-life (~7h → ~30+ h), (5) appears to reduce hERG and cardiac liability — making noribogaine the safer therapeutic candidate currently in clinical development for opioid use disorder (DemeRx, etc.). The 18-MC (18-methoxycoronaridine) congener was designed to retain anti-addictive efficacy while reducing tremor, hERG, and Purkinje toxicity by altering scaffold geometry.
